title: Sanders amendment: Most Favored Nation drug pricing
question: On the Motion to Waive All Applicable Budgetary Discipline Re: Sanders Amdt. No. 5159 to S.Con.Res. 33 (budget resolution)
yes_means: Yes was a vote to let the Senate consider an amendment to cut U.S. prescription drug prices by more than half by capping them at the prices paid in Europe and Canada (Most Favored Nation pricing). It needed 60 votes and the vote tied 49-49.
industry_position: PhRMA, the drugmakers' trade group, lobbied members of Congress to resist legislation that would write Most Favored Nation drug pricing into law.

title: Add an extension of the expanded ACA premium tax credits to H.R. 1
question: On the Motion to Waive Section 302(f) of the Congressional Budget Act Re: S.Amdt. 2696 to H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to let the Senate add an extension of the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, paid for by a higher tax rate on income over $10 million, to the 2025 budget reconciliation bill. It needed 60 votes and got 47.
industry_position: AHIP, the health insurers' trade group, urged Congress to extend the enhanced premium tax credits before they expired at the end of 2025.

title: House gives final approval to H.R. 1
question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment to H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to send the Senate-passed budget reconciliation bill, with its Medicaid work requirements, Medicaid financing limits and new marketplace enrollment rules, to the President to become law.
industry_position: After the Senate passed the bill, AHIP warned it could bring the biggest rollback in health coverage in U.S. history and urged Congress to change course.

title: Extend the expanded ACA premium tax credits
question: On the Cloture Motion to proceed to S. 3385
yes_means: Yes was a vote to move forward a bill extending for three years the enhanced premium tax credits that lower the cost of Affordable Care Act marketplace insurance. It needed 60 votes and got 51.
industry_position: AHIP urged Congress to extend the enhanced premium tax credits, paired with added program-integrity measures, for the 24 million people relying on them.

title: House passes a three-year extension of the expanded ACA premium tax credits
question: On Passage of H.R. 1834, the Breaking the Gridlock Act
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass a bill extending the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits for three years. It reached the floor through a discharge petition and passed 230-196.
industry_position: AHIP urged Congress to extend the enhanced premium tax credits, paired with added program-integrity measures, for the 24 million people relying on them.

title: House passes H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Passage of H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass the House version of the 2025 budget reconciliation bill. Its health provisions included new Medicaid work requirements and limits on how states finance their share of Medicaid, including a freeze on provider taxes.
industry_position: The American Hospital Association urged the House to reject the bill's Medicaid and marketplace cuts, which it said would cut federal Medicaid support by more than $700 billion.

title: Kim amendment: strike H.R. 1's limits on Medicaid payments
question: On the Amendment S.Amdt. 2817 to H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to remove the bill's limits on certain Medicaid payments to states and providers, which hospitals said would cut what Medicaid pays them.
industry_position: The American Hospital Association asked senators to change the bill's limits on state-directed payments and provider taxes, which it said went far beyond the House bill.

title: Senate passes H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Passage of the Bill H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass the 2025 budget reconciliation bill, which added Medicaid work requirements and limits on provider taxes and state-directed payments. It passed 50-50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.
industry_position: The American Hospital Association urged the Senate to reject the bill unless it was changed, warning its limits on provider taxes and state-directed payments would close hospitals, especially in rural areas.

title: House passes sanctions on the International Criminal Court
question: On Passage of H.R. 23, the Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass a bill imposing sanctions on people who help the International Criminal Court investigate or prosecute Americans or citizens of allied countries, including Israel.
industry_position: AIPAC supported the bill and commended the House for passing it.

title: Advance sanctions on the International Criminal Court
question: On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed to H.R. 23
yes_means: Yes was a vote to begin debate on the House-passed bill imposing sanctions on people who help the International Criminal Court investigate or prosecute Americans or citizens of allied countries, including Israel. It needed 60 votes and got 54.
industry_position: AIPAC supported H.R. 23 and commended the House for passing it before the Senate vote.

title: Sanders resolution: block an arms sale to Israel (April 2025)
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 33
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed U.S. sale of defense articles and services to Israel. It failed 15-82.
industry_position: AIPAC urged its members to oppose the Sanders resolutions and praised the Senate for rejecting them.

title: Greene amendment: cut $500 million in Israel missile-defense funding
question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (Greene, Part A Amendment No. 114) to H.R. 4016, Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
yes_means: Yes was a vote to strike $500 million for U.S.-Israel cooperative missile-defense programs from the 2026 defense spending bill. It failed 6-422.
industry_position: AIPAC called the amendment reckless and welcomed its defeat.

title: Sanders resolution: block a sale of assault rifles to Israel
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 41
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed export of defense articles to Israel, reported as tens of thousands of automatic assault rifles. It failed 27-70.
industry_position: AIPAC opposed the resolutions and praised the Senate for again rejecting Sanders' attempt to ban the weapons sales.

title: Sanders resolution: block a sale of bulldozers to Israel
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 32
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed U.S. sale of defense articles to Israel, reported as military bulldozers. It failed 40-59.
industry_position: AIPAC called the resolutions misguided and dangerous and thanked the senators who voted against them.

title: Sanders resolution: block a sale of bombs to Israel
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 138
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed U.S. sale of defense articles to Israel, reported as 1,000-pound bombs. It failed 36-63.
industry_position: AIPAC called the resolutions misguided and dangerous and thanked the senators who voted against them.

title: Repeal EPA methane fee on oil and gas producers
question: On Passage, H.J.Res. 35
yes_means: A Yes vote backed using the Congressional Review Act to cancel EPA's rule carrying out the Waste Emissions Charge, the fee on methane from large oil and gas facilities that leak above a set threshold.
industry_position: API wanted the fee repealed, calling it a duplicative, punitive tax on U.S. energy production, and praised the House and Senate for passing the resolution.

title: Repeal EPA methane fee on oil and gas producers
question: On the Joint Resolution, H.J.Res. 35
yes_means: A Yes vote sent the resolution cancelling EPA's methane Waste Emissions Charge rule to the President.
industry_position: API wanted the fee repealed, calling it a duplicative, punitive tax on U.S. energy production, and praised final congressional passage.

title: Overturn California's gas car phase-out waiver (Advanced Clean Cars II)
question: On Passage, H.J.Res. 88
yes_means: A Yes vote backed cancelling the EPA waiver that let California require all new cars sold in the state to be zero-emission by 2035, a rule other states had adopted too.
industry_position: API and the refiners' group AFPM backed the resolution as a win for consumers and urged the Senate to finish overturning what they call California's gas car ban.

title: Overturn California's gas car phase-out waiver (Advanced Clean Cars II)
question: On the Joint Resolution, H.J.Res. 88
yes_means: A Yes vote sent the President the resolution cancelling the EPA waiver behind California's 2035 zero-emission new car requirement.
industry_position: API and AFPM applauded the Senate vote, arguing California regulators should not decide what cars Americans can buy.

title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act, final House passage
question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment, H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote gave final approval to the 2025 reconciliation law and sent it to the President. Among much else, it mandates regular onshore and offshore oil and gas lease sales and phases out many clean energy tax credits.
industry_position: API called the law the most important energy bill in a generation, citing its 30 required Gulf lease sales, quarterly onshore lease sales and tax treatment of oil and gas investment.

title: SPEED Act: narrow federal environmental reviews for energy projects
question: On Passage, H.R. 4776
yes_means: A Yes vote passed a bill that amends the National Environmental Policy Act to shorten and narrow federal environmental reviews and set firm deadlines for permits on projects such as pipelines.
industry_position: API backed the bill as a commonsense step toward fixing a broken federal permitting system and praised its House passage.

title: Repeal CFPB $5 cap on big-bank overdraft fees
question: On the Joint Resolution, S.J.Res. 18
yes_means: A Yes vote backed cancelling the CFPB rule that would have capped overdraft fees at very large banks at about $5 or required them to charge no more than cost.
industry_position: The American Bankers Association called the overdraft rule unlawful government price-setting that would force banks to limit or drop overdraft coverage, and applauded the Senate vote to repeal it.

title: Repeal CFPB $5 cap on big-bank overdraft fees
question: On Passage, S.J.Res. 18
yes_means: A Yes vote sent the President the resolution cancelling the CFPB overdraft fee cap for very large banks.
industry_position: The ABA endorsed the resolution, and its CEO said Congress had acted to right a wrong done by the CFPB.

title: Repeal OCC rule tightening review of bank mergers
question: On the Joint Resolution, S.J.Res. 13
yes_means: A Yes vote backed cancelling the Comptroller of the Currency's 2024 rule that raised scrutiny of proposed bank mergers, and bars the OCC from issuing a substantially similar rule without new authority from Congress.
industry_position: The ABA backed the resolution, said mergers need clear, transparent standards, and urged the House to act quickly.

title: Repeal OCC rule tightening review of bank mergers
question: On Passage, S.J.Res. 13
yes_means: A Yes vote sent the President the resolution cancelling the OCC's 2024 bank merger review rule.
industry_position: The ABA sent a letter urging House support, arguing the OCC ignored concerns raised before adopting the rule and that repeal lets regulators rethink merger policy.

title: Rand Paul amendment to end Fed interest payments to banks on reserves
question: On the Amendment, S. 2296 (FY2026 NDAA)
yes_means: A Yes vote supported Sen. Paul's amendment to bar the Federal Reserve from paying banks interest on reserve balances held at the Fed. It failed 14-83.
industry_position: The ABA and 52 state bankers associations told Senate leaders to reject the amendment, arguing it would not cut federal spending and would hurt small banks most.

title: House passes FY2026 defense policy bill (NDAA)
question: On Passage, H.R. 3838
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the House version of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act. The bill sets Pentagon policy and authorizes spending levels, and it includes changes to how the Pentagon buys weapons.
industry_position: The Aerospace Industries Association endorsed H.R. 3838 when the Armed Services Committee marked it up. It backed the bill's faster acquisition rules and higher procurement thresholds as good for the defense industrial base.

title: Senate passes FY2026 defense policy bill (NDAA)
question: On Passage of the Bill, S. 2296
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the Senate version of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, which authorizes Pentagon programs and spending.
industry_position: AIA praised Senate passage on the day of the vote and pressed Congress to put broad acquisition reform into the final bill.

title: House passes final FY2026 NDAA
question: On Passage, S. 1071 (final FY2026 NDAA text)
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the final House-Senate compromise of the FY2026 NDAA, about $900 billion in defense authorizations. The text rode on S. 1071 and went back to the Senate.
industry_position: AIA commended Congress for passing the FY2026 NDAA. It said the bill supports troops and strengthens the defense industrial base.

title: Senate clears final FY2026 NDAA
question: On the Motion, S. 1071 (final FY2026 NDAA)
yes_means: A Yes vote gave final Senate approval to the House-Senate compromise FY2026 NDAA and sent it to the President.
industry_position: AIA issued a statement the same day commending Congress for passing the bill. It said the bill would speed innovation across the defense sector.

title: House passes FY2026 Pentagon spending bill
question: On Passage, H.R. 4016
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the House's FY2026 Department of Defense appropriations bill, which funds the Pentagon, including weapons procurement.
industry_position: AIA welcomed House passage. It also said the topline was too low for current threats and asked Congress to raise it.

title: House passes final FY2026 spending package including Pentagon funding
question: On Passage, H.R. 7148
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026. It carried the final $839 billion FY2026 defense appropriations along with several other agencies' budgets.
industry_position: AIA urged swift passage of the FY2026 defense funding bill. It cited stable funding for industry and continued multiyear buys of munitions.

title: Senate passes FY2026 spending package including Pentagon funding
question: On Passage of the Bill, H.R. 7148
yes_means: A Yes vote passed an amended version of the FY2026 consolidated appropriations package. The package included full-year Defense Department funding and went back to the House.
industry_position: AIA called for quick enactment of the FY2026 defense appropriations in this package so contractors would have predictable funding.

title: House passes FY2027 defense policy bill (NDAA)
question: On Passage, H.R. 8800
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the House FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act, which authorizes a record of about $1.15 trillion in military spending.
industry_position: AIA endorsed the House Armed Services Committee's FY2027 NDAA when it was released, praising its commercial-buying, acquisition and supply-chain provisions (its statement covers the committee text).

title: House passes One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Passage, H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the House version of the budget reconciliation bill. It extended the 2017 tax cuts and cut Medicaid and SNAP.
industry_position: The AFL-CIO urged a No vote. It argued that the bill's tax benefits go mostly to the wealthy while Medicaid, SNAP and federal worker pension cuts would cost jobs.

title: Senate passes One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Passage of the Bill, H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the Senate's amended reconciliation bill: tax cut extensions paid for partly by Medicaid and SNAP cuts. The Vice President broke the 50-50 tie.
industry_position: In a June 28 letter, the AFL-CIO urged senators to vote no. It cited health coverage losses, SNAP cuts, job losses and a tax tilt toward the richest households.

title: House gives final approval to One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment, H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote accepted the Senate's version of the reconciliation bill and sent it to the President to become law.
industry_position: AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler asked House members to vote no on the Senate amendment. She warned of job losses from the bill's Medicaid, SNAP, ACA and clean energy credit cuts.

title: House passes Protect America's Workforce Act
question: On Passage, H.R. 2550
yes_means: A Yes vote passed a bill to cancel President Trump's executive orders that removed union bargaining rights from most federal employees.
industry_position: AFSCME, along with other federal-sector unions, backed the bill to restore bargaining rights for about one million federal workers and welcomed its passage.

title: House passes Faster Labor Contracts Act
question: On Passage, H.R. 5408
yes_means: A Yes vote passed a bill that requires employers to start bargaining within 10 days of a union win. Stalled first-contract talks would go to mediation and then binding arbitration.
industry_position: The Teamsters led the push for the bill and called it the most important labor bill in decades. They are now pressing the Senate to pass it.

title: Senate confirms Lori Chavez-DeRemer as Labor Secretary
question: On the Nomination, PN114 (Lori Chavez-DeRemer, Secretary of Labor)
yes_means: A Yes vote confirmed Lori Chavez-DeRemer, a former House member with a pro-union record, as Secretary of Labor.
industry_position: The Teamsters backed her from the start and praised her confirmation. They criticized the senators who voted against her.

title: Senate confirms Boeing labor lawyer Scott Mayer to NLRB
question: On the Nomination, PN252 (Scott Mayer, NLRB Member)
yes_means: A Yes vote confirmed Scott Mayer, Boeing's chief labor counsel, to the National Labor Relations Board. His seat restored the board's quorum with a Republican majority.
industry_position: The AFL-CIO urged senators not to confirm Mayer. It cited his work for Boeing and an anti-union law firm, and doubts that he would stay independent of the White House.

title: GENIUS Act stablecoin bill, Senate passage
question: On Passage of the Bill, S. 1582
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the GENIUS Act, which sets the first federal rules for payment stablecoins, and sent it to the House.
industry_position: The Blockchain Association praised the Senate vote. It called the bill the first standalone pro-crypto bill to pass the Senate and a win for American crypto developers and businesses.

title: GENIUS Act stablecoin bill, House final passage
question: On Passage, S. 1582
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the Senate's stablecoin bill without changes and sent it to the President, who signed it into law.
industry_position: The Blockchain Association welcomed the bipartisan House vote as the first full federal framework for stablecoins and asked the President to sign the bill quickly.

title: CLARITY Act crypto market structure, House passage
question: On Passage, H.R. 3633
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the CLARITY Act, which divides oversight of crypto markets between the SEC and CFTC and sets registration rules for crypto firms. It went to the Senate.
industry_position: The Blockchain Association backed House passage because it wanted market structure rules for the crypto industry, and said it would work with the Senate on the bill.

title: Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, House passage
question: On Passage, H.R. 1919
yes_means: A Yes vote passed a bill that bars the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency directly to individuals.
industry_position: The Blockchain Association praised the House vote to restrict a U.S. central bank digital currency, saying it protects privacy, competition and financial freedom.

title: CLARITY Act, Senate motion to begin debate
question: On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed, H.R. 3633
yes_means: A Yes vote would have ended debate on taking up the crypto market structure bill so the Senate could consider it. It got 49 votes and needed 60, so it failed.
industry_position: The Blockchain Association, Crypto Council for Innovation, Ripple and Coinbase-backed Stand With Crypto all wanted the bill to advance and criticized the failed vote.

title: Repeal IRS DeFi broker reporting rule, Senate
question: On the Joint Resolution, S.J.Res. 3
yes_means: A Yes vote used the Congressional Review Act to overturn an IRS rule that would have required decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms to report users' crypto transactions as brokers.
industry_position: Blockchain Association members wrote to Congress asking for a Yes vote on S.J.Res. 3, arguing the DeFi broker rule would harm the industry.

title: Repeal IRS DeFi broker reporting rule, House
question: On Passage, H.J.Res. 25
yes_means: A Yes vote overturned the IRS rule requiring DeFi platforms to report users' crypto transactions as brokers. This version later passed the Senate and became law.
industry_position: The Blockchain Association applauded the enactment of the resolution and called the broker rule a misguided last-minute Biden administration regulation.

title: Strip state AI law moratorium from the One Big Beautiful Bill
question: On the Amendment (to strike the section relating to support for artificial intelligence), H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote removed the provision that would have blocked states from enforcing their own AI laws as a condition of federal funding. It passed 99-1.
industry_position: NetChoice asked the Senate to keep the temporary pause on state AI regulation in the reconciliation bill, arguing a patchwork of state rules would slow American AI.

title: TAKE IT DOWN Act, House final passage
question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, S. 146
yes_means: A Yes vote made it a crime to publish nonconsensual intimate images, including AI deepfakes, and required platforms to remove them within 48 hours of a request. It went to the President.
industry_position: Meta, Google, Amazon, X and the trade group TechNet signed a letter to House leaders urging passage to protect victims of image-based abuse.

title: One Big Beautiful Bill with $0 suppressor and short-barreled rifle tax, Senate passage
question: On Passage of the Bill, H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the reconciliation bill. Among many other provisions, it cut the $200 federal tax on suppressors, short-barreled rifles and shotguns, and other NFA items to $0. It passed 51-50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.
industry_position: The NRA supported the bill because it removed the NFA tax on suppressors and short-barreled firearms, and it urged members to push for a Yes vote.

title: One Big Beautiful Bill with $0 suppressor and short-barreled rifle tax, House final passage
question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment, H.R. 1
yes_means: A Yes vote accepted the Senate's version of the reconciliation bill and sent it to the President. The bill included cutting the NFA tax on suppressors and short-barreled firearms to $0.
industry_position: The NRA praised final passage because of the language it had backed cutting the NFA tax stamp to $0, and it described this as a first step toward ending the NFA.

title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act, House passage
question: On Passage, H.R. 1041
yes_means: A Yes vote barred the VA from reporting a veteran to the federal gun background check system (NICS) only because a fiduciary manages the veteran's benefits.
industry_position: The NRA and NSSF both supported the bill. They said veterans should not lose gun rights without due process just because the VA manages their benefits.

title: Confirm Robert Cekada as ATF Director
question: On the Nomination, PN730-14 (Robert Cekada, ATF Director)
yes_means: A Yes vote confirmed Robert Cekada as Director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. He was confirmed 59-39.
industry_position: The National Shooting Sports Foundation, the gun industry's trade group, sent a letter of strong support for Cekada and praised his confirmation, saying he respects Second Amendment rights.

title: KIDS Act (kids online safety package)
question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended, H.R. 7757
yes_means: A Yes vote passed a package of 14 children's online safety bills. It sets new requirements for social media platforms, AI chatbots and parental controls.
industry_position: NetChoice opposed the package, calling it unconstitutional, saying it treats legal speech as harmful and gives federal agencies backdoor authority over content moderation, and faulting it for not preempting state laws.

title: Repeal CFPB oversight of Big Tech payment apps
question: On Passage, S.J.Res. 28
yes_means: A Yes vote repealed the CFPB rule that brought large digital wallet and payment app providers (Apple Pay, Google Pay and others) under federal supervision and examination.
industry_position: NetChoice and TechNet had sued to block the CFPB rule. NetChoice praised Congress for passing the repeal and urged the President to sign it.

title: Repeal CFPB oversight of Big Tech payment apps
question: On the Joint Resolution, S.J.Res. 28
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the resolution to repeal the CFPB rule that put large digital payment apps and wallets under federal supervision.
industry_position: NetChoice and TechNet sued to block the rule and dropped the suit after Congress repealed it, calling the repeal the decisive blow against regulatory overreach.

title: SPEED Act (NEPA permitting overhaul)
question: On Passage, H.R. 4776
yes_means: A Yes vote passed a bill that narrows and speeds up federal environmental reviews under NEPA for energy projects, data centers and other infrastructure.
industry_position: OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Vantage Data Centers, the Data Center Coalition and tech trade groups are on the committee's supporter list; OpenAI wrote that faster permitting is needed to build data centers and the power plants behind them.

title: Housing for the 21st Century Act
question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended, H.R. 6644
yes_means: A Yes vote passed the House's bipartisan housing supply bill, covering zoning, permitting, manufactured housing and HUD program changes.
industry_position: The National Association of Realtors applauded House passage, calling the bill a meaningful bipartisan step on housing affordability.

title: Amended 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree, H.Res. 1299 (H.R. 6644)
yes_means: A Yes vote sent the Senate a revised housing bill that dropped the Senate's forced sale of build-to-rent homes and kept limits on large investors buying single-family homes.
industry_position: A coalition including NAHB, NMHC, NAA, Nareit, MBA and the Real Estate Roundtable backed the amended bill because it removed the build-to-rent sale mandate.

title: ROAD to Housing Act final passage
question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur, H.R. 6644
yes_means: A Yes vote gave final congressional approval to the housing supply package and sent it to the President.
industry_position: NAHB praised the deal, saying it would expand housing supply by cutting regulatory barriers and pushing local zoning reform, after lobbying to keep the build-to-rent sale mandate out.

title: Cloture on final ROAD to Housing Act deal
question: On the Cloture Motion, H.R. 6644 (SA 5823)
yes_means: A Yes vote ended debate so the Senate could approve the final House-Senate housing deal.
industry_position: The National Association of Realtors backed the final package, calling it the most significant housing legislation to pass Congress in nearly 20 years.

title: Senate approves final ROAD to Housing Act deal
question: On the Motion to Concur, H.R. 6644 (SA 5823)
yes_means: A Yes vote approved the final negotiated housing package in the Senate and sent it back to the House for the last vote.
industry_position: NAR supported the final housing package as the biggest housing bill in nearly two decades; NAHB also applauded its passage.

title: Homeowner Energy Freedom Act
question: On Passage, H.R. 4758
yes_means: A Yes vote repealed Inflation Reduction Act programs, including $1 billion for states that adopt the 2021 model energy code for new homes.
industry_position: NAHB made passage a key vote, saying the 2021 energy code can add more than $20,000 to the price of a new home.

title: Affordable HOMES Act (manufactured home energy rules)
question: On Passage, H.R. 5184
yes_means: A Yes vote voided the Energy Department's 2022 efficiency standards for manufactured homes and gave HUD sole authority over them.
industry_position: The Manufactured Housing Institute applauded passage, saying the bill ends duplicate DOE and HUD oversight of manufactured home energy standards.
